description: Doom level design rubric. Heuristics are strict (v0.2); scores 4-5 need human/VLM.

visual_hierarchy.title: Visual Hierarchy
visual_hierarchy.prompt: Does the level use lighting, color, or landmarks to draw the eye toward the objective?

signposting.title: Signposting
signposting.prompt: Are paths clearly defined with visual cues that reduce backtracking?

breadcrumbs.title: Breadcrumbs
breadcrumbs.prompt: Does exploration yield micro-rewards that confirm a valid path?

intensity_curve.title: Intensity Curve
intensity_curve.prompt: Does the level balance high-stress moments with recovery and exploration?

choke_points_and_arenas.title: Choke Points and Arenas
choke_points_and_arenas.prompt: Are spaces sized for their function (cover/flanks in arenas; distinct transitions)?

symmetry_vs_asymmetry.title: Symmetry vs. Asymmetry
symmetry_vs_asymmetry.prompt: For multiplayer, is the map balanced? For single-player, is spatial variety intentional?

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.prompt: Does the level safely introduce a new mechanic or hazard?

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.prompt: Does it test the mechanic with enemies, motion, or time pressure?

subversion.title: Subversion
subversion.prompt: Does a late twist force a creative reuse of the mechanic?

readability.title: Readability
readability.prompt: Can a player look at an asset and know what it does?

consistency.title: Consistency
consistency.prompt: Do identical-looking surfaces behave the same across the map?

sense_of_place.title: Sense of Place
sense_of_place.prompt: Does the level feel like a lived-in world rather than generic corridors?

showing_vs_telling.title: Showing vs. Telling
showing_vs_telling.prompt: Can room history be read from debris, blood, or abandoned items without a text log?
